page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core allocation. Storage includes a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network performance features a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across general compute and memory evaluations. The system scored 1580.0 on Geekbench single-core and 9632.0 on multi-core tests, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 21159.7 and a PassMark memory score of 2483.45. Memory bandwidth reaches 89.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 54.02 GB/sec for uncached writes. CPU-driven inference benchmarks reflect average results across most model sizes, though text generation on a 135M parameter LLM performed strongly at 265.24 tokens per second. Redis SET operations measured at 15.8 million operations per second, supported by 21.51 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The qualitative profile of the r6idn.4xlarge balances high memory density with high-speed local NVMe storage and 25 Gbps network bandwidth. This combination offers high operational resource density for systems that require both extensive volatile memory and fast local scratch space, eliminating network storage bottlenecks. Given the dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and local NVMe capacity, the instance is well suited for in-memory databases, large Redis clusters, high-throughput database operations, caching tiers, and data processing ETL pipelines.

With an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local disk storage, the r6idn.4xlarge is tailored for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, distributed caches, and analytical ETL processing.
